storyboard.claim: A barista order is the empty bar: the lightest first rep of saying no.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener at a cafe counter, a confident half-smile, a cup in hand, ready for the easy first rep.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ends the previous beat's gym lesson: start with the empty bar.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: places the empty-bar idea in an everyday cafe.
storyboard.staging: The listener at a cafe counter, a confident half-smile, a cup in hand, ready for the easy first rep.

storyboard.claim: Practise saying no to a clerk: eye contact, the word, no apology.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener facing the viewer and pointing firmly, level gaze, no flinch.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the empty-bar practice from the barista.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the three parts of the act: eye contact, the word no, no apology.
storyboard.staging: The listener facing the viewer and pointing firmly, level gaze, no flinch.

storyboard.claim: Each no retrains the fear centre: walking away brings no punishment.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener walking away relaxed and smiling, nothing bad following.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the practice in the previous beat matters.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the amygdala as what the practice retrains.
storyboard.staging: The listener walking away relaxed and smiling, nothing bad following.

storyboard.claim: Block the tiny withdrawals now to protect the principle when stakes are massive.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener gripping a shield with a determined scowl, guarding against small drains.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the everyday refusals to the money-like account of small costs.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links small refusals to protecting what matters later.
storyboard.staging: The listener gripping a shield with a determined scowl, guarding against small drains.

storyboard.claim: Habit makes the brain not freeze when the VP asks for weekend work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener frozen in thought beside the brisk boss with a tablet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the workplace stake that the practice prepares for.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the boss as the source of the request the listener must refuse.
storyboard.staging: The listener freezes as the boss makes the request.

storyboard.claim: The hosts will raise one honest criticism of the whole philosophy.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator speaking to the audience in an abstract stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition from the practice section to the critique.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals that the summary is turning from advice to critique.
storyboard.staging: A host speaks directly, framing the turn.

storyboard.claim: The book suggests that choosing the right words alone makes refusals painless.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator talking, setting up the claim being examined.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the critique by naming the book's claim.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the book's suggestion directly before testing it.
storyboard.staging: A host states the claim to be examined.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the idea that guilt neatly evaporates.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumped and sad: no magic relief, the guilt stays.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the book's claim that wording removes guilt.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the magic promise as the narrator's rejection.
storyboard.staging: The listener slumped and sad: no magic relief, the guilt stays.

storyboard.claim: Guilt lingers and gnaws; it does not vanish on command.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener staring worriedly at a phone, replaying the refusal, unable to let go.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the rejection of the magic promise.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows guilt gnawing after the refusal, not vanishing.
storyboard.staging: The listener staring worriedly at a phone, replaying the refusal, unable to let go.

storyboard.claim: Saying no to the wrong executive can cost a promotion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss pointing across the office, the cost of a refusal.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the first real cost of refusing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the career consequence for a refusal to an executive.
storyboard.staging: The boss stands as the figure who decides promotions.

storyboard.claim: Refusing a friend can end the calls.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon with the friend looking sad.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the work cost to the personal cost.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the friendship consequence of a refusal.
storyboard.staging: The friend holds a phone that will stop ringing.

storyboard.claim: The book's advice can strain at the extremes and sanitize human interaction.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator talking, presenting the critique.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the critique with the book's limits.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the sanitized view of human interaction as the flaw.
storyboard.staging: A host delivers the critique directly.

storyboard.claim: A boundary can reveal a relationship that was transactional rather than mutual.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A sorter splitting mutual affection from transactional ties.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains how a boundary exposes the relationship's true basis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sorts the two possible kinds of relationship the boundary reveals.
storyboard.staging: Diagram: relationships sorted by their basis.

storyboard.claim: Discovering the relationship was only transactional is a real grieving loss.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener slumped in sadness while the boss turns away with her tablet.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the sorted relationship: the loss is real.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the loss in a person walking away, not just a mood.
storyboard.staging: The listener slumped in sadness while the boss turns away with her tablet.

storyboard.claim: Saying yes to everything makes you a servant to other people's priorities.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A chains icon for being bound to other people's demands.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the alternative to losing a relationship.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the life of constant yes as servitude.
storyboard.staging: Chains show being bound to others' priorities.

storyboard.claim: Plating the toxic boss slowly costs you yourself.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener with a blank, emptied face holding a mask, the boss beside them satisfied.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the trade-off between relationships and self.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the self hollowing out behind a pleasing front.
storyboard.staging: The listener with a blank, emptied face holding a mask, the boss beside them satisfied.

storyboard.claim: A yes must be weighed against its cost.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance icon weighing two sides.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the people the listener admires.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames each yes as a weighing.
storyboard.staging: The listener thinks, weighing the scales.

storyboard.claim: The admired people are protective of their time, not yes-sayers to every request.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shield icon for protecting time and energy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the admired people from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the protective stance as the trait to admire.
storyboard.staging: A shield stands for the protected time.

storyboard.claim: The narrator rejects the idea that the aim is hoarding time out of stinginess.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The narrator talking, rejecting the hoarding reading.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the core thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the stingy reading of boundaries.
storyboard.staging: A host rejects the hoarding reading.

storyboard.claim: Spend your currency where it matters; a no is not rudeness.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener choosing deliberately, pointing with a wallet in hand.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the core thesis as spending.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames a no as a deliberate spending choice.
storyboard.staging: The listener choosing deliberately, pointing with a wallet in hand.

storyboard.claim: A no is the only way to keep the yeses you actually mean.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener smiling, holding a gift they chose to give freely.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the payoff of the thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the kept yes as a gift given by choice.
storyboard.staging: The listener smiling, holding a gift they chose to give freely.

storyboard.claim: The people you fear disappointing may respect you more after a clear no.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The boss with a small approving smirk, tablet down, facing the listener.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the reader with a hypothetical.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the feared person's possible respect.
storyboard.staging: The boss with a small approving smirk, tablet down, facing the listener.

storyboard.claim: Closing the vault with courage makes your currency valuable.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The listener pointing sharply with a resolute face, a key in hand to lock the vault.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the chunk with the courage that makes yeses valuable.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names courage as the act that gives boundaries worth.
storyboard.staging: The listener pointing sharply with a resolute face, a key in hand to lock the vault.
